SM10-01.solved: 2/7 = 0.285714 repeating, cycle (2,8,5,7,1,4) of length 6. 50 mod 6 = 2, so the 50th digit is the 2nd of the cycle = 8.
SM10-01.note: All five options are digits drawn from the actual cycle, so no option-set narrowing is possible. The stem hands the student the period (6), which removes the one genuinely hard step; that is fine for SSAT but makes this a modular-arithmetic item rather than a repeating-decimal item.

SM10-02.solved: 12 notebooks = 4 groups of (2 paid + 1 free), so 8 are paid for. 8 x 3.60 = 28.80.
SM10-02.note: 32.40 (=9 x 3.60, off-by-one grouping), 43.20 (=12 at full price) and 21.60 (=6) are all real wrong paths.

SM10-03.note: 20 is the reversed-base error (9/45) and 80 is 36/45; both are exactly the errors this stem is built to catch. Clean item.

SM10-04.note: 7 in the option set is the median itself, which is a fair trap. 4.5 and 8 are not reachable from any wrong path I can name; they are filler.

SM10-05.solved: The triangle's base (6) lies on one 12 cm side and its apex on the opposite 12 cm side, so its height is the 8 cm separation. Area = 1/2 x 6 x 8 = 24. Rectangle = 96. 24/96 = 1/4.
SM10-05.note: Geometry is fully determined by the stem without a figure - the apex position along the side does not change the area, which is the point. 3/8 (= 48/96, forgetting the 1/2) is the intended slip.

SM10-06.solved: 1 cm represents 5 km, so 1 cm^2 represents 25 km^2. 18 x 25 = 450.
SM10-06.note: 90 (= 18 x 5, linear factor applied to an area) is the classic error and is present. Good item.

SM10-07.note: 26 (stopping at 2n) and 33 (stopping at the numerator) are both intermediate values, which is exactly the right distractor family for a reverse-operations item.

SM10-08.solved: x + y = 28 and y + z = 44. Subtracting, z - x = 16.
SM10-08.note: 8 (the difference of the two averages, i.e. forgetting to double) is the intended slip and is present.

SM10-09.solved: (2,1) and (11,1) give a horizontal base of 9; the third vertex at y = 7 gives a height of 6. Area = 1/2 x 9 x 6 = 27.
SM10-09.note: 54 (forgot the 1/2) present. Routine once the horizontal base is spotted.

SM10-10.note: 24 (stopping at 3h) and 62 (the common cost, answering a question that was not asked) are both good. Note this is the fourth item in the batch that reduces to one small linear equation (see 03, 07, 08) - the batch is thin on variety, not on quality.

SM10-12.solved: Trailing zeros of 25! = floor(25/5) + floor(25/25) = 5 + 1 = 6 (twos are in surplus).
SM10-12.note: Genuinely hard for this exam: the student must know zeros come from 5x2 pairs AND that 25 contributes a second 5. 5 is the answer for anyone who misses only the second point, which is the majority. This is the one item in the batch where two ideas have to interact.

SM10-13.note: 48 is the total volume of the mixture (right work, wrong question) - strong. 13.5 is the 45 percent of 30 intermediate.

SM10-15.note: 54 (ignoring the cut) and 51 (subtracting the side length 3 instead of the area 9) are real; 18 and 42 are weak filler. Fine as an opener.
